strategy.summary: Reproduce an accuracy regression in scikit-learn’s RidgeCV when using gcv_mode="svd" with extremely small alphas on noiseless data; the project’s own Ridge/GCV regularization-limit test should fail on the buggy commit and pass on the fixed revision.

pinned_because: Pin scikit-learn to the buggy commit c83733128e2c (transition point for the numerical behavior).

Use a NumPy version at/above the project’s documented minimum, because the documented dependency constraint is explicitly numerically relevant for this repro (RidgeCV relies on NumPy linear algebra/numerics).
Use SciPy at/above its documented minimum; even if the failing path is primarily NumPy-backed, the documented dependency constraint is numerically relevant for scikit-learn in general.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision, running the repository test above should fail an assert_allclose that expects RidgeCV with alpha near 0 to recover the (near) LinearRegression coefficients/intercept in noiseless data for gcv_mode="svd"; on the fixed revision, the same test should pass for both gcv_mode values (with the same random split/generation and tolerances).
strategy.numerical_probe: The test checks correctness by asserting RidgeCV.coef_ and RidgeCV.intercept_ match the expected values from a helper that reduces to LinearRegression for alpha near zero (alpha values include 1e-16). The failure mode described in the issue is catastrophic coefficients and thus the test’s coefficient/intercept allclose should fail (no separate score/printing assertions are required).

input_output_examples.input: alphas=[1e-15, 1e-14]; RidgeCV(alphas=alphas, gcv_mode="svd").fit(X_train, y_train); score = ridge_cv.score(X_test, y_test) with make_regression(n_samples=1000, n_features=50, noise=0, random_state=42) and train_test_split(test_size=0.9, random_state=42)

risks: This repro is sensitive to floating-point dtype: the test parametrizes dtype over np.float32 and np.float64; if the bug only manifests in float32 (the issue text suggests float32/numerical stability concerns), ensure you run the full parametrization and don’t override dtype in the local run.

The evidence mentions array-api/dtype casting constraints (notably torch+mps disallowing float64). This strategy relies on the standard NumPy-based test path (the test file uses numpy/scipy arrays). If you run under a nonstandard array namespace or device, results may differ.

Sparse containers are parameterized as [np.asarray] + CSR_CONTAINERS in the test. The test file includes skips for gcv_mode="svd" with sparse X. The failing transition should therefore be exercised for dense (np.asarray) inputs; if you only run a subset, include dense cases.

Potential architecture/toolchain dependence: if the underlying numerical failure depends on BLAS/LAPACK implementation (OpenBLAS/MKL) or CPU instruction sets, ensure the same dependency stack between buggy and fixed runs.

oracle.reference_source: Project test oracle: test_regularization_limits_ridge_gcv uses _ridge_regularization_limits(alpha, X, y, fit_intercept) which returns LinearRegression fit results when alpha is near 0, and then assert_allclose(gcv_ridge.coef_, expected_coef, atol=1e-5 if dtype==float32 else 1e-10) and same for intercept_.
oracle.why: The test does not compare RidgeCV score directly; it compares coefficients/intercept against a deterministic reference computed by LinearRegression on noiseless data.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The test’s assert_allclose on RidgeCV.coef_ and RidgeCV.intercept_ for (gcv_mode="svd", alpha=1e-16, fit_intercept={True,False}, X_container=np.asarray, dtype in {float32,float64}, X_shape in {(100,50),(50,50),(50,100)}) should fail because RidgeCV in svd mode selects/uses an ill-conditioned computation at extremely small alpha, producing coefficients with wildly incorrect magnitude (as described: extremely large |coef| leading to catastrophic metrics).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying the fix from the referenced PR, the same parameter combinations should yield coefficients/intercept that match the LinearRegression reference within the test’s dtype-dependent tolerances, so assert_allclose succeeds.
